symbols.name: Flat-bottomed flask
symbols.draw: Same neck and bulb radius as roundBottomFlask. Move the circle's centre down until the circle cuts y = h in a chord 0.5w long. That chord is the flat base. Join it to the circle with radius 6 fillets.

symbols.name: Pear-shaped flask
symbols.draw: Neck 34 wide and 0.25h high, 3 u rim flare. Body: one smooth pear outline from the neck to a round bottom; widest (w) at 0.68h; the bottom is an arc of radius 0.3w. Two cubic curves each side; no corner at the joins.

symbols.name: Volumetric flask
symbols.draw: Bulb: a circle of radius 0.44w whose centre is 0.36w above y = h, so the flat base is a chord about 0.5w long; radius 6 fillets at the base. Neck 18 wide from y = 0 down to the bulb, with a 2 u rim flare and radius 10 fillets where it meets the bulb. Mark: detail line across the neck at 0.2h. Stopper: plug 22 wide and 14 high above the rim, role solid.

symbols.name: Büchner flask
symbols.draw: As conicalFlask, with the standard 34 u neck. Side arm: tube 8 wide and 22 long on the right of the neck at y = 0.14h, pointing right, open end. The cavity stops at the neck wall.
symbols.label: Büchner flask

symbols.name: Side-arm boiling tube
symbols.draw: As boilingTube. Side arm: tube 8 wide and 20 long on the right at y = 0.16h, pointing right, open end. The cavity stops at the tube wall.

symbols.name: Crystallising dish
symbols.draw: Straight walls, flat base, corner radius 8. The left rim turns out 5 u as a spout.

symbols.name: Evaporating basin
symbols.draw: Shallow bowl with a flat foot. Each wall is one quadratic curve from the rim (0.5w from the centre, y = 0) to the foot end (0.15w from the centre, y = h); its control point is at (0.5w from the centre, y = h). The foot is a straight line between the foot ends. The left rim turns out 6 u as a spout.

symbols.name: Crucible
symbols.draw: Tapered cup: rim width w, base width 0.55w, base corner radius 5. Lid: shallow arc 1.1w wide resting on the rim, with a 6 u knob, role solid.

symbols.name: Watch glass
symbols.draw: One arc from (-w/2, 0) to (w/2, 0) that dips to (0, h). Line only. Two base anchors: `under` at (0, h) for a glass that stands on a surface, and `edge` at (0, 0) for a glass that rests on a rim with its bowl inside the mouth.

symbols.name: Polystyrene cup
symbols.draw: Tapered cup: rim width w, base width 0.68w. Thick wall: outer and inner outline 5 u apart, closed at the rim, role solid. Lid: slab 6 u thick and w + 8 wide with a centre hole 10 wide (two pieces, as bung).

symbols.name: Reagent bottle
symbols.draw: Cylinder body, base corner radius 8. Shoulders of radius 14 into a neck 26 wide and 0.16h high, 3 u rim flare. Stopper: plug with a flat round head, role solid.

symbols.name: Wash bottle
symbols.draw: Bottle as reagentBottle with a neck 22 wide. Cap: rect 28 by 12, role solid. Delivery tube: glass tube 5 wide from 12 u above the base, up through the cap, then bent to run 34 u down-left to a jet.

symbols.name: Gas jar
symbols.draw: Straight cylinder, flat base, corner radius 4. Rim: flat flange 5 u out on each side. Lid: glass plate w + 16 wide and 3 u thick, role solid.

symbols.name: U-tube
symbols.draw: Tube 24 wide inside. Two upright arms joined by a half-circle bend; outer bend radius w/2. 2 u rim flare on each arm.
symbols.label: U-tube

symbols.name: Displacement can
symbols.draw: Cylinder, flat base, corner radius 4. Spout: tube 9 wide that leaves the right wall at y = 0.22h and slopes down 30 degrees for 30 u, open end. The cavity is the can only: it stops at the wall. A can that is full to the spout has amount 0.75.

symbols.name: Calorimeter (metal can)
symbols.draw: Straight can, flat base, corner radius 3, no lip.

symbols.name: Measuring cylinder
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Burette
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Thermometer
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Pipette
symbols.draw: Tube 6 wide. Bulb 20 wide and 70 long centred at 0.5h, with smooth shoulders. Mark: detail line across the stem at 0.16h. The lower 26 u tapers to a 2.5 u jet.

symbols.name: Dropping pipette
symbols.draw: Glass tube 8 wide; the lower 30 u tapers to a 2.5 u jet. Teat: rounded bulb 16 wide and 30 high at the top, role rubber.

symbols.name: Gas syringe
symbols.draw: Drawn lying down, nozzle to the left. Nozzle: tube 7 wide and 16 long that starts at x = -w/2. Barrel: 0.45w long and 34 high, closed at the nozzle end and open at the other. Plunger: one rigid part. Its piston is a slab 5 u thick inside the barrel, plunger × the barrel length from the closed end. Its rod is 6 wide and as long as the barrel. Its flange, 30 high, is at the end of the rod. So at plunger = 0 the flange is just outside the barrel, and at plunger = 1 it is at the right edge of the box. Scale: 20 divisions along the barrel (5 cm³ each), a long tick every fourth; `numbers` adds 0 to 100 in steps of 20, size 8, under the barrel. The cavity is the gas space between the closed end and the piston. The Reading field (0 to 100 cm³) sets plunger = reading / 100.

symbols.name: Syringe
symbols.draw: Upright plastic syringe, nozzle down. Barrel 20 wide and 0.5h long with a finger flange at the top; nozzle 4 wide and 12 long. Plunger: one rigid part, as gasSyringe: at plunger = 0 the piston is at the nozzle end; at plunger = 1 its flange is at y = 0.

symbols.name: Balance
symbols.draw: Pan: slab 0.7w wide and 5 high at the top of the box. Stem: 10 wide and 6 high under the pan centre. Body: from y = 11 to h, top edge 0.86w wide, base w wide, corner radius 4, role solid. Display: rect 54 by 16 on the front of the body, with the reading as symbol text, size 10.

symbols.name: Stopwatch
symbols.draw: digital: case, a rounded rect w by 0.84h at the bottom of the box, corner radius 8, role solid; display, a rect 0.76w by 0.34h in the upper half of the case, with the reading as symbol text, size 9; two buttons, rects 10 by 6, on the top edge of the case. analogue: circle of radius 0.44w centred at (0, h - 0.46w), role solid; crown, a rect 8 by 9 on top; twelve detail ticks inside the rim and one hand from the centre; no reading text.

symbols.name: Ruler
symbols.draw: Rect, role solid. Ticks on the top edge: each cm 8 u long, each 5 cm 12 u long. For 100 cm: each 10 cm long, each 1 cm short only when the spacing is 3 u or more. Numbers, size 8, under the long ticks.

symbols.name: Newton meter
symbols.draw: Body: rect 22 wide from y = 14 to 0.72h, role solid, with 10 scale divisions. Ring at the top: circle radius 6. Pointer: short heavy line across the body at `reading`. Rod from the pointer to a hook below the body.

symbols.name: Meter box
symbols.draw: Box, corner radius 6, role solid. Display window 0.6w by 22 with the reading as symbol text, size 12. Title as symbol text, size 10, under the display. terminals = 2: two circles of radius 4 on the lower edge at x = 0.3w each side (anchors `a:terminal`, `b:terminal`). terminals = 4: two input terminals at the lower left and two output terminals at the lower right (anchors `inA`, `inB`, `outA`, `outB`, all `terminal`). The label text is the `title` parameter.
symbols.label: pH meter

symbols.name: Probe
symbols.draw: Rod 8 wide with a rounded tip, role solid. Cap 12 by 16 at the top, role dark.

symbols.name: Light gate
symbols.draw: Upside-down U that stands on the bench: a bar 14 high across the top and two arms 10 wide from the bar down to y = h, one outline, role solid. Beam: dashed line between the arms at 0.37h, where the card on a trolley cuts it.

symbols.name: Pipette filler
symbols.draw: Bulb: circle of radius 0.44w at the top, role rubber. Sleeve: a tube below the bulb that narrows from 14 wide to 9 wide and ends at y = h, role rubber. Valve: a small disc of radius 4 where the bulb meets the sleeve, role solid.

symbols.name: Magnified scale
symbols.draw: A section of a scale, for reading questions. Tube: two upright wall lines 0.5w apart, centred, from y = 0 to h. Each end is a wavy break line, role detail. Scale: `divisions` equal divisions between the value `top` at y = 14 and the value `bottom` at y = h - 14; ticks on the left wall, long at each end and at the middle; the two end values as symbol text, size 10, left of the wall. If `top` equals `bottom`, draw as if `bottom` were `top` + 1. The cavity is the space between the walls; the scale is tied to it, so the Reading field sets the liquid level. For a burette `top` is the smaller value.

symbols.name: Bunsen burner
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.
symbols.label: Bunsen burner

symbols.name: Tripod
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Gauze
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Heatproof mat
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Spirit burner
symbols.draw: Squat bottle: body 0.9w wide and 0.5h high, corner radius 10; short neck 22 wide. Wick holder: rect 14 by 8, role solid. Wick 4 wide. Flame: the shape of the bunsenBurner safety flame, 22 high, role flame, tint #f7d26a.

symbols.name: Heat arrow
symbols.draw: Block arrow pointing up: shaft 16 wide, head 40 wide and 26 high, role solid. The word under it as symbol text, size 13.

symbols.name: Pipeclay triangle
symbols.draw: Heavy line with three tube beads: rects 14 by 6, role solid.

symbols.name: Hot plate
symbols.draw: Box, corner radius 5, role solid. Top plate: slab 0.9w by 7 above the box, role dark. Two dials: circles of radius 7 on the front. stirrer: the second dial has a short pointer line. The label text is `magnetic stirrer` when `stirrer` is on.

symbols.name: Heating mantle
symbols.draw: Casing: box with corner radius 8, role solid. Its top edge dips into a bowl: a half-circle recess of radius 55 centred at (0, 0), drawn as part of the one casing outline. The cup anchor is at the bottom of the bowl, (0, 55). Dial: circle of radius 7 on the front, at (0.38w, 0.78h).

symbols.name: Water bath (electric)
symbols.draw: Tank: open-top vessel inset 10 u from each side, from y = 0 to 0.7h, corner radius 6. The tank is the cavity. Casing: one outline with no fill (role outline) from the tank rim down the outside to y = h, corner radius 6. Control strip: the lowest 0.22h of the casing, role solid, with a dial (circle of radius 7) and a detail line along its top edge.

symbols.name: Immersion heater
symbols.draw: Rod 12 wide with a rounded lower end, role dark. Cap 16 by 18 at the top, role solid, with two lead stubs 10 u long.

symbols.name: Bung
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Clamp stand
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Boss and clamp
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Test-tube rack
symbols.draw: Front view. Two end plates 8 wide and full height, role solid. Top bar at y = 0.25h and bottom bar at y = h - 8, each 8 high, role solid. Holes: `holes` of them, at a pitch of (w - 16) / holes. The top bar has a gap for each hole (pieces, as bung): 26 wide for test tubes and 38 wide for boiling tubes, but never more than the pitch - 6. One cup anchor on the bottom bar under each hole: `slot1` to `slot<holes>`.

symbols.name: Test-tube holder
symbols.draw: Wooden holder: two arms that meet at the left end and grip at the right. Spring: small rect at 0.6w, role solid.

symbols.name: Bench
symbols.draw: Heavy line at y = 0, full width. Under it: detail hatch lines at 45 degrees, 8 u apart, 10 u long.

symbols.name: Cotton wool plug
symbols.draw: Cloud outline: 7 to 9 small arcs round an oval, role solid.

symbols.name: Lid
symbols.draw: Slab, corner radius 2, role solid. holes = 1: a centre gap 10 wide. holes = 2: two gaps 10 wide at x = 0.22w each side. Draw the slab in pieces, as bung, and give each gap a port anchor (`hole1`, `hole2`).

symbols.name: Glass rod
symbols.draw: Rect with rounded ends (radius 3), role solid.

symbols.name: Spatula
symbols.draw: Flat blade 14 wide and 40 long at the lower end with a rounded tip, narrowing to a handle 5 wide. Role solid.

symbols.name: Splint
symbols.draw: Thin rect 4 high, role solid. lit: a small flame 16 high at the right end, the shape of the bunsenBurner safety flame, role flame, tint #f7d26a. glowing: a dark-role dot of radius 3 at the right end with three short detail rays.

symbols.name: Filter paper
symbols.draw: A V of two dashed lines from the rim points (w/2 each side, y = 0) to (0, h). residue: stipple dots in the lowest third.

symbols.name: Chromatography paper
symbols.draw: Rect, role solid. Baseline: detail line 18 u above the bottom edge. Samples: `spots` of them, evenly spaced along the baseline, each with its own tint. developed off: each sample is a dot of radius 3 on the baseline. developed on: each start position is a small pencil cross (two detail lines 4 u long), and each sample has 1 to 3 dots above its cross, in a fixed pattern by index, all below the solvent front. Solvent front: dashed line at `front` of the way from the baseline to the top. plate: a second line 3 u inside the left edge. The label text is `TLC plate` when `plate` is on.

symbols.name: Capillary tube
symbols.draw: Tube 5 wide, closed and round at the lower end. Sample: dark-role fill in the lowest 8 u.

symbols.name: Magnetic stirrer bar
symbols.draw: Capsule: rounded rect of radius 4, role solid.

symbols.name: White tile
symbols.draw: Slab, corner radius 1.5, role solid.

symbols.name: Spotting tile (top view)
symbols.draw: Rounded rect of radius 8, role solid. Wells: circles of radius 0.3 × the cell size on a rows × cols grid, role solid. iodine: every well gets the tint #b98556 (iodine solution), and the first `blueBlack` wells, counted row by row, get the role dark with the tint #3b4a6b (starch is present).

symbols.name: Paper with cross
symbols.draw: Paper in oblique view: a parallelogram with its bottom edge from (-w/2, h) to (w/2 - 18, h) and its top edge from (-w/2 + 18, 0) to (w/2, 0), role solid. Cross: two heavy lines 10 u long that form an X centred at (0, 0.72h). The surface anchor is at (0, 0.45h): a flask that stands there hides the back of the paper and leaves the cross in view.

symbols.name: G-clamp
symbols.draw: Frame, role solid: a bar 8 thick down the left side, with a jaw 8 thick at the top and at the bottom that reach 0.6w to the right. Screw: rod 5 wide up through the lower jaw, with a pad 12 wide at its top end and a T-bar handle 20 wide at its bottom end.
symbols.label: G-clamp

symbols.name: Filter funnel
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.

symbols.name: Büchner funnel
symbols.draw: Top: straight walls w wide and 0.38h high. Perforated plate: dashed line across at 0.38h. paper: a detail line 2 u above the plate, full width (the filter paper). Below the plate a cone narrows to a stem 9 wide at 0.66h. The stem runs to h and is cut at an angle. The cavity is the space above the plate only, from 1.5 u below the rim to 0.38h.
symbols.label: Büchner funnel

symbols.name: Separating funnel
symbols.draw: Neck 22 wide and 0.1h high. Pear body: widest (w) at 0.3h, narrowing to the tap at 0.74h. Tap: body rect 14 by 14 with its key to the right, as burette. Stem 6.4 wide from the tap to h, cut at an angle. Stopper: plug 26 wide and 16 high with a flat head, role solid. The cavity ends at the tap.

symbols.name: Dropping funnel
symbols.draw: Cylinder body w wide from 0.1h to 0.6h with round shoulders. Neck 22 wide. Tap and stem as separatingFunnel.

symbols.name: Thistle funnel
symbols.draw: Cup: w wide and 26 high, bowl-shaped, on a small bulb 18 wide. Stem 7 wide to h.

symbols.name: Liebig condenser
symbols.draw: Pilot: see src/symbols/pilots.ts.
symbols.label: Liebig condenser

symbols.name: Still head
symbols.draw: Upright tube 28 wide, centred at x = -w/2 + 17. Top: socket (34 wide at its mouth, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) at y = 0, for the thermometer adaptor. Bottom: cone joint (34 wide at its shoulder, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) that ends at y = h. Side arm: tube 13 wide that leaves the right side of the upright tube at 0.3h and slopes down 18 degrees for 70 u, then widens to a cone joint (34 wide at its shoulder, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) in line with the arm. The cavity is the upright tube only.

symbols.name: Receiver adaptor
symbols.draw: Bent tube. Its socket (34 wide at its mouth, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) is at the upper left, and its axis slopes down 18 degrees to the right. Past the socket the tube narrows to 13 wide, bends smoothly (centre-line radius 20) until it points straight down, and ends as an outlet 10 wide at (0.25w, h), cut at an angle. The cavity is the tube after the socket.

symbols.name: Thermometer adaptor
symbols.draw: Lower part: cone joint (34 wide at its shoulder, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) from y = 10 to h. Cap: rubber-role rect 38 by 10 on top. A centre hole 9 wide runs through both, so draw each in two pieces, as bung. The plug anchor is at the cone shoulder.

symbols.name: Fractionating column
symbols.draw: Tube 30 wide with a socket (34 wide at its mouth, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) at the top and a cone joint (34 wide at its shoulder, narrowing to 28 over 24 u) at the bottom. Packing: lumps drawn by the symbol in the middle 70 %, from the kernel rng with a fixed seed.

symbols.name: Melting point apparatus
symbols.draw: Box, corner radius 8, role solid. Heating block: dark-role rect 0.5w by 0.3h near the top with two holes in its top edge (thermometer 9 wide, capillary 5 wide), each with a mouth anchor. Viewing lens: circle of radius 12 on the front. Dial: circle of radius 9 with a pointer.

symbols.name: Electrode
symbols.draw: rod: rect 8 wide, centred, with a rounded lower end. strip: rect 16 wide, the full box. carbon: role dark. metal: role solid.

symbols.name: Electrolysis cell
symbols.draw: Open vessel with straight walls from y = 0 to h - 16, corner radius 6, no lip. Two electrodes: dark-role rods 8 wide at x = 0.22w each side, from 0.45h down through the vessel base to y = h - 4. Base seals: rubber-role rects 14 by 8 where each rod passes the base. Feet: two solid-role rects 10 wide from the vessel base to y = h, at x = 0.42w each side. The terminals are the lower ends of the rods.

symbols.name: Power supply
symbols.draw: Box, corner radius 6, role solid. Dial: circle of radius 14 with a pointer. Terminals: circles of radius 5 at the lower right, marked + and - with symbol text, size 11. Voltage as symbol text, size 10, above the dial.

symbols.name: Crocodile clip
symbols.draw: Two jaws that meet at the left, each with three zigzag teeth on its inner edge. The body narrows to a wire stub at the right.

symbols.name: Salt bridge
symbols.draw: Upside-down U tube, 14 wide inside, outer corners of radius 16. Both ends open and pointing down.

symbols.name: Trolley
symbols.draw: Body: rect w by 26 from y = 0, corner radius 3, role solid. Wheels: two circles of radius 10 centred at (0.3w each side, h - 10), role solid, drawn over the body, each with a hub dot. Hook: small heavy line at the right end. card: rect 30 by 26 that stands on the top of the body, above the box, role solid.

symbols.name: Bench pulley
symbols.draw: Wheel: circle of radius 16 centred at (6, 18) with a hub dot. Bracket: bar from the hub down-left to a clamp block 16 by 30, role solid, with a 6 u slot on its left side for the bench edge.

symbols.name: Masses on a hanger
symbols.draw: Hook at the top (small arc). Rod 3 wide down to a base disc 30 by 5. Masses: slabs 36 by 8 stacked on the disc, role dark.

symbols.name: Spring
symbols.draw: Zigzag of `coils` turns between y = 14 and y = h - 14, full width, round joins. A straight 8 u tail and a loop (circle of radius 4) at each end.

symbols.name: Metal block
symbols.draw: Block, role solid, with two blind holes from the top: heater hole 16 wide and 0.78h deep at x = -0.2w; thermometer hole 10 wide and 0.6h deep at x = 0.22w. Draw one outline that goes down into each hole. Each hole has a mouth anchor at its top, so a heater or a thermometer snaps to its centre line. insulated: an outer jacket 9 u from the block on the sides and bottom, dashed.

symbols.name: Leslie cube
symbols.draw: Square can: straight walls, flat base, corner radius 2. Lid: slab w + 6 wide and 6 high with a filler cap 12 wide, role solid.
symbols.label: Leslie cube

symbols.name: Infrared detector
symbols.draw: Box 0.7w by h, corner radius 4, role solid. Snout 0.3w by 16 on the left that ends in a dark-role window 4 wide.

symbols.name: Ripple tank
symbols.draw: Tray: shallow open vessel w by 26 at y = 0.42h on two legs that reach h. Lamp: bulb (circle of radius 9) on a rod 0.32h above the tray centre, with three dashed rays down to the tray. Dipper: bar 0.3w long that touches the water at the left, hung from a motor box 26 by 18. Screen: slab 0.9w by 5 at y = h, role solid.

symbols.name: Vibration generator
symbols.draw: Box, corner radius 6, role solid. Pin: rod 4 wide and 16 high above the top centre, with a small hook. Two terminals: circles of radius 4 on the front.

symbols.name: Wooden bridge
symbols.draw: Triangle with a 2 u flat top, role solid.

symbols.name: Lamp
symbols.draw: Base: slab 0.7w by 8, role solid. Stem: rod 5 wide rising to a holder 18 by 14. Bulb: circle of radius 16 centred at (0.15w, 0.2h), facing right. rays: five detail lines 14 u long fanning out to the right of the bulb.

symbols.name: Irregular solid
symbols.draw: Closed blob: 9 points round an ellipse, radii varied by a fixed pattern (0.8 to 1.0), joined with fillets of radius 5, role rubber.

symbols.name: Microscope
symbols.draw: Side view, eyepiece at the upper left. Base: foot slab 0.8w by 12, role solid. Arm: curved bar rising from the back of the base to 0.25h. Stage: slab 0.55w by 6 at 0.62h with a clip. Body tube: rect 22 wide, leaning 25 degrees from upright, from the arm top to the eyepiece (rect 16 by 18). Nosepiece: disc under the tube with two objective lenses (rects 10 by 24 and 10 by 16) that point at the stage. Focus knobs: circles of radius 9 and 6 on the arm. Lamp: half-circle of radius 10 on the base under the stage.

symbols.name: Microscope slide (side view)
symbols.draw: Slab 3 u thick, role solid. Cover slip: slab 0.25w by 2 centred on top. Specimen: dark-role line under the cover slip.

symbols.name: Petri dish (top view)
symbols.draw: Two circles (radius w/2 and w/2 - 5), role solid. colonies: dark dots of radius 2 at fixed pseudo-random places. discs: solid-role circles of radius 7 on a ring of radius 0.27w, each with a dashed clear-zone circle of radius 14.
symbols.label: Petri dish

symbols.name: Quadrat (top view)
symbols.draw: Square frame: two squares 5 u apart, role solid. Grid: detail lines that divide the inside into grid × grid cells.

symbols.name: Pondweed
symbols.draw: Stem: one smooth S-curve from the cut end at (0, h) to the tip at (0, 0), main line. Leaves: pairs of small pointed ovals 9 by 4 every 10 u along the stem, angled 40 degrees towards the tip, role solid.

symbols.name: Potato cylinder
symbols.draw: Rounded rect of radius 5, role solid.

symbols.name: Leaf
symbols.draw: Two mirrored curves from the stalk at (0, h) to the tip at (0, 0), widest (w) at 0.55h, role solid. Midrib and three vein pairs as detail lines. Stalk 10 u.

symbols.name: Cell
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Long plate (positive): main line 24 high at x = -3. Short plate (negative): main line 12 high at x = 3. Both plates have the same line weight.

symbols.name: Battery
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Two cells in line that face the same way, joined by a dashed line. Terminals at (40 each side, h/2).

symbols.name: Switch
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Two contacts: circles of radius 2.5, role solid, at x = 12 each side. Open: the lever rises 30 degrees from the left contact. Closed: the lever lies on both contacts.

symbols.name: Lamp (symbol)
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Circle of radius 12 with an X inside that reaches the circle.

symbols.name: Fuse
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Rect 30 by 12 with the lead line running through it.

symbols.name: Resistor
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Rect 30 by 12. The leads stop at the rect.

symbols.name: Variable resistor
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Resistor with a diagonal arrow through it, from lower left to upper right.

symbols.name: Thermistor
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Resistor with a diagonal line through it that ends in a short level foot at the lower left. circle: a circle of radius 19 round the symbol.

symbols.name: LDR
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Resistor with two small parallel arrows that point at it from the upper left. circle: a circle of radius 19 round the symbol. The arrows start outside the circle.
symbols.label: LDR

symbols.name: Diode
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Triangle 16 wide that points right, with a bar 16 high at its tip. The lead line runs through. circle: a circle of radius 14 round the symbol.

symbols.name: LED
symbols.draw: Circuit symbol. Terminals a and b at (30 each side, h/2); leads run from them to the symbol. Diode with two small parallel arrows that point away at the upper right. circle: a circle of radius 14 round the symbol. The arrows start outside the circle.

symbols.name: Bohr atom
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. Bohr (shell) diagram of element z, and of the ion when charge is not 0 (the same engine as the inventory row ionShell). Data: ELEMENTS and ionShells in elements.ts (for an impossible charge draw the neutral atom). The atom fills its box: the outermost shell is a circle of radius w/2 minus 8 u (a further 18 u smaller when charge is not 0, to leave room for the brackets); the n shells are evenly spaced between the nucleus (radius 14 u, role solid) and that circle, role detail. Electrons: evenly spaced on each shell, the first at the top, marks from electrons.ts (dot = role ink, cross = role detail). Nucleus text: the element symbol (nucleus symbol, 16 u), or the proton and neutron counts on two lines (numbers: 'Z p' over 'N n', neutrons = a - z from elements.ts, 11 u), or nothing. outerOnly draws only the outermost shell and its electrons round the nucleus. otherMarks gives the last k electrons of the outer shell the other mark (the electron that moves when an ion forms). structure writes the electron structure (shellString, 12 u) under the atom and shrinks the atom by 14 u to make room. An ion is drawn inside large square brackets (bracketD) with the charge as superscript text at the top right outside them (size 16, markup: 2^+). Label: element name + ' atom' or ' ion'. The science checks (electrons = Z - charge; shell counts equal ionShells; the shells fill 2, 8, 8, 2) are tested in atoms.science.test.ts, from a model that atoms.ts exports.
symbols.label: sodium atom

Plum pudding: a large circle (role tint, with its hatch) and the electrons scattered inside it by a fixed pattern, each marked as `mark` says (minus = a short detail line; dot; cross); no nucleus. Nuclear: a very small nucleus (radius 4 u, role dark) in the middle with a plus sign beside it and the electrons on one wide ring (radius 0.42w). Shell: the nucleus with up to 2 shells as bohrAtom (2 electrons then the rest). No text except the plus and minus signs; labels are label items. Label: 'plum pudding model', 'nuclear model' or 'shell model'. Science: the plum pudding has no separate nucleus; in the nuclear and shell pictures every electron is outside a nucleus much smaller than the atom; the electron count equals the parameter.

symbols.name: Nuclide notation
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Text only: the element symbol (24 u) with the mass number above the atomic number to its left (16 u, right-aligned with each other), and the charge as a superscript (markup) at the right when it is not 0. a = 0 means the mass number of the commonest isotope (elements.ts); an a smaller than z is raised to z. counts adds three short lines under it: 'Z protons', 'N neutrons', 'E electrons' (12 u; E = z - charge). The box is the nominal size; the counts may stick out below. Label: element name and mass number, for example 'sodium-23'. symbols.name: Isotopes (nuclei)
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. One to three nuclei side by side (a2 or a3 of 0 means none), each a tight hexagonal cluster of a circles of radius 5 u: z protons (role tint, with a plus sign) and a - z neutrons (role solid, plain), laid out from the middle outwards so that every circle can be counted and the clusters never overlap. Under each cluster (when notation is on) the nuclide notation of nuclideNotation (the same code, not a copy of it); with counts, the proton and neutron counts. a1, a2 and a3 below z are raised to z. Label: element name + ' isotopes'. Science: the circles in a cluster number a; z of them are protons; isotopes of one element share z.

symbols.name: Alpha particle scattering
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. On the left a lead block with a slit (role solid) and an arrow for the beam; in the middle a thin gold foil as a vertical column of small circles (the atoms, radius 6 u) with a nucleus dot (radius 1.5 u, role ink) in each when nuclei is on; round the foil a curved detector screen (role dashed arc, radius 0.45h). `paths` alpha paths as lines with arrowheads (detail): most go straight through, some bend a little away from the nearest nucleus (like charges repel), one reverses; a fixed pattern, never random. Paths that bend are bent more the closer they pass; no path enters a nucleus. No text; labels are label items. Label: default.

symbols.name: Periodic table
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. The standard layout of 18 columns by 4 rows of square cells 28 u wide (the cells that no element of the range fills stay empty; hydrogen and helium are at the two ends of period 1). Each cell: its outline (detail) and, per `content`, the symbol (14 u), the atomic number (9 u above), both, the relative atomic mass (9 u below, from elements.ts `ar`), or nothing (a blank worksheet). Group numbers above the columns (KS4 numbering 1 to 7 and 0, from ks4Group, or IUPAC 1 to 18, or none) and period numbers 1 to 4 at the left (11 u). hlGroup (IUPAC 1 to 18), hlPeriod and hlElement (a ring round one cell): at most one highlight. A stepped divider line (heavy) between metals and non-metals, when on. shading: regions of metals or of blocks use tint plus hatch (never colour alone). The element data is elements.ts (the first 36 elements); the eight cells of the d-block are Sc to Zn. Label: default. Science: elements run in order of atomic number; helium is in group 0 (KS4); the transition metals are in IUPAC groups 3 to 12 of period 4; the divider runs between the right pairs of cells.

symbols.name: Ionic dot-and-cross diagram
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. The ratio of ions follows the charges (Mg and Cl: one Mg2+ and two Cl-; Na and O: two Na+ and one O2-; Al and O: two Al3+ and three O2-). stage 'transfer': each atom as a circle for its outer shell (inner shells only when `inner` is on, as plain circles), the metal's outer electrons as the first mark and the non-metal's as the second, and a curved arrow from each metal electron to the non-metal. stage 'ions': each ion inside square brackets (bracketD) with its charge as superscript text; the metal ion shows no outer electrons (empty outer shell, or the inner shell when `inner` is on), the non-metal ion a full outer shell of both marks. Marks (S6, decision 4): default = metal dots and non-metal crosses, swapped = the other way, ring = dots and small open rings; always black, so one picture serves slides and photocopies. The diagram is laid out across the box and scales to fit. Data: elements.ts and ionShells. Label: the compound name, for example 'sodium chloride' (metal name + non-metal name with the ending -ide). Science: electrons lost = electrons gained; every ion has a noble gas structure; the numbers of ions give a neutral compound; the charge follows the group.
symbols.label: sodium chloride

symbols.name: Covalent dot-and-cross diagram
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. Outer shell only, never the inner shells. The 13 molecules form the small-molecule library: put its data (atoms with their element, the bonds with their order, the lone pairs) in src/symbols/molecules.ts, exported, for later symbols (displayed formula, ball-and-stick) to share. layout 'overlap': one circle for the outer shell of each atom, overlapping where atoms are bonded; each shared pair sits in the overlap as one mark of each kind; the other outer electrons stay on the atom's own circle, lone pairs as pairs; a double or triple bond has two or three pairs in the overlap; the central atom is in the middle for H2O, NH3, CH4 and CO2; C2H4 and C2H6 have two carbon atoms side by side. layout 'apart': the atoms apart with their shared pairs between them. Marks (decision 4): the first atom of the formula (or the central atom) uses crosses and the atoms bonded to it dots; in a molecule of two identical atoms one atom uses dots and the other crosses; swapped and ring as ionicDotCross. All in black. Label: the molecule name, for example 'water'. Science: every atom ends with a full outer shell (2 for hydrogen, 8 for the others); the pairs shared equal the valency; the total outer electrons equal the sum over the atoms; lone pairs are drawn.
symbols.label: water

symbols.name: Particle box
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. A box (role outline) holding particles that never overlap (radius 7 u for the larger kind, 5 u for the smaller; fixed pattern from the seed of kernel/geom.ts rng, never Math.random). substance: element = one kind of single atom; molecules = joined pairs of one kind (H2, O2); compound = touching groups of two or three atoms of two kinds in the ratio of `formula` (AB, AB2, A2B); mixtureElements = two kinds of free atom; mixtureCompounds = two kinds of molecule that are not bonded to each other; mixtureElementCompound = free atoms and molecules. The kinds differ by size and fill: A white (role solid), B tint with hatch, C solid ink (S6, S12). state: solid = a regular lattice in contact, filling the lower rows; liquid = touching, irregular, filling the lower two thirds; gas = spaced widely through the whole box. motion adds a short arrow on some particles (longer for a gas); the arrows never cross a particle. `count` is the number of particles (a molecule counts as one). Label: 'particle diagram'. Science: every particle of an element is one kind; each compound unit holds the atoms of its formula in the right ratio; a mixture has at least two kinds and no bond between them; circles never overlap; a solid is a lattice in contact; a gas has gaps larger than a particle. AS BUILT (release 1.2; the model is particleModel() in src/symbols/matter.ts): radii 7 u (A, C) and 5 u (B) at full size; a box too small for the count draws all particles smaller by one common factor (steps of 0.94, floor 0.3), so that circles never overlap and the three states keep one size. A molecule in a solid or liquid keeps a hairline of 3 u (times that factor) from the next molecule, so that each can be counted. The liquid is a touching, irregular heap on the floor, at most two thirds of the box high. compound = AB (A-B), AB2 (B-A-B at 104.5 degrees) or A2B (A-B-A); mixtureCompounds = compound(A,B) + compound(C,B) of one formula; mixtureElementCompound = free C + compound(A,B). The count is shared evenly between the kinds. Motion arrows are on about half of the units (three quarters in a gas), 9 u long in a solid or liquid and 20 u in a gas, clear of every circle. Minimum size 120 by 90.
symbols.label: particle diagram

symbols.name: Reaction profile
symbols.draw: The row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json holds the drawing, the parameters and the science checks that a test must make; this row fixes the contract. Release 1.2 (priority C). Rules S6, S11 (relaxed) and S14 of docs/SPEC.md apply; fills are the roles tint, hatch (photocopy-safe) and ink; shared code: src/symbols/elements.ts, electrons.ts, kit.ts, kernel/hatch.ts. Two axes (outline, with arrowheads): energy up the side, progress of reaction along the bottom, with the words 'Energy' and 'Progress of reaction' as symbol text (rotated text is not possible: put 'Energy' above the vertical axis). A smooth curve from a flat reactants level to a rounded peak and down to a flat products level; exothermic = products below the reactants, endothermic = above; the peak is above both. levels: 'reactants' and 'products' (words), or the labels as lines to write on (blank). activation: a double-headed arrow from the reactants level to the peak. change: a vertical arrow between the two levels, down for exothermic and up for endothermic. catalyst: a second, lower, dashed peak (role dashed). Label: 'reaction profile'. Science: exothermic has products below reactants; the catalysed peak is lower, with the same start and end. AS BUILT (release 1.2; the model is profileModel() in src/symbols/energy.ts): `formulae` shows two worked examples, balanced: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O (exothermic) and CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2 (endothermic); `blank` draws two lines of 80 u to write on. The reactants level is carried across to the change arrow by a dashed line, and the activation arrow stands under the apex. Labels go below their plateau, except the products of an endothermic reaction (above). The curve is two cubic Beziers with level tangents, so it has no kink. Minimum size 230 by 160.
symbols.label: reaction profile

symbols.draw: A common iron nail for rusting and displacement experiments: a flat round head 12 wide and 3 high at the top, a shank 4 wide down to a point over the last 8 u. Role solid. Symmetric about x = 0 (S8). Release 1.2 (priority C).

symbols.name: Ionic lattice (3D)
symbols.draw: PILOT PICTURE, built in release 1.2: James approves the style of this picture (decision 3) before the structures and molecule packs are built. The model (pure data) and the drawing are in src/symbols/lattices.ts and lattices.science.test.ts tests the model and that the drawing agrees with it; the head of the file lists the departures from the first brief. The inventory row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json says what the course asks. Rules S6 and S12 (tint with hatch), S14 (the oblique projection: oblique() in src/symbols/oblique.ts). GEOMETRY. A 3 by 3 by 3 block of sodium chloride: 27 ions at the integer points (i, j, k), each 0 to 2 (i along x, j up, k away from the viewer). Cl- (tinted) where i + j + k is even (14 ions); Na+ (white) where it is odd (13 ions). Spacing 48.8 u and radii 7.5 u (Cl-) and 4.8 u (Na+) at the default size 150, scaled with w / 150; outlines 2 u. (The first brief's 44, 11 and 7 made neighbouring circles overlap by 3.8 u.) 54 bonds between unlike ions (distance 1 along x, y or z), trimmed to the circle edges, role detail; the three bonds on the hidden back corner (i = 0, j = 0, k = 2) are role dashed. Bonds are drawn first, then the circles. With `bonds` off the picture shows the 27 circles only. No text. Label: 'ionic lattice'.
symbols.label: ionic lattice

symbols.name: Diamond (giant covalent)
symbols.draw: PILOT PICTURE, built in release 1.2: James approves the style of this picture (decision 3) before the structures and molecule packs are built. The model (pure data) and the drawing are in src/symbols/lattices.ts and lattices.science.test.ts tests the model and that the drawing agrees with it; the head of the file lists the departures from the first brief. The inventory row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json says what the course asks. Rules S6 and S12 (tint with hatch), S14 (the oblique projection: oblique() in src/symbols/oblique.ts). GEOMETRY. A cluster of 17 carbon atoms: the central atom C0 at the origin; its 4 neighbours at u d_a (d1 = (1, 1, 1), d2 = (1, -1, -1), d3 = (-1, 1, -1), d4 = (-1, -1, 1)); and from each neighbour its 3 other neighbours (12 atoms). u = 24 u at the default size 160. The model is turned 20 degrees about the vertical axis before the projection, so that no circles overlap (the first brief allowed 15: the circles are then 5.5 u apart; at 20 they are 10.9 u apart). White circles of radius 7 u. 16 bonds trimmed to the circle edges: heavy (role outline) when the bond points to the viewer, thin (role detail) when it points away (mid-point at z greater than 0). Painter order, far to near. `stubs` (default on): each of the 12 outer atoms has its 3 missing bonds as stubs, a fixed 5 u past the circle edge that does not scale with the box, role detail, so that every atom shows four bonds. No text. Label: 'diamond'.

symbols.name: Buckminsterfullerene (C60)
symbols.draw: PILOT PICTURE, built in release 1.2: James approves the style of this picture (decision 3) before the structures and molecule packs are built. The model (pure data) and the drawing are in src/symbols/cages.ts and cages.science.test.ts tests the model and that the drawing agrees with it; the head of the file lists the departures from the first brief. The inventory row of the same id in spec/diagrams.json says what the course asks. Rules S6 and S12 (tint with hatch), S14 (the oblique projection: oblique() in src/symbols/oblique.ts). GEOMETRY. The truncated icosahedron: 60 vertices (all cyclic permutations of (0, +-1, +-3 phi), (+-1, +-(2 + phi), +-2 phi) and (+-phi, +-2, +-(2 phi + 1)); edge length 2), 90 edges, 12 pentagons (centres along (0, +-1, +-phi) and its cyclic permutations) and 20 hexagons (along (+-1, +-1, +-1) and the cyclic permutations of (0, +-phi, +-1/phi); the first brief had the mirror family (0, +-1/phi, +-phi), which picks out one atom). View: one pentagon turned to the viewer (a corner pointing down), then 14 degrees about x and 10 degrees about y; orthographic; ball radius 0.44 w. A face faces the viewer when the cosine of its normal with the line of sight is more than 0.3 (the first brief had 0: faces seen almost edge-on drew doubled lines and overlapping circles at the rim); an edge is visible when it lies on a face that faces the viewer; hidden edges are omitted (an opaque ball), so there are 30 atoms, 40 bonds and 11 faces. White circles of radius 3.8 u; bonds role outline, trimmed to the circle edges; drawn far to near. With `pentagons` on (default off) the visible pentagons are tinted() polygons behind the bonds. No text. Label: 'buckminsterfullerene'.
symbols.label: buckminsterfullerene
